cues.text: Making something smaller or shorter is almost always possible. Making it bigger or longer depends on what is hidden inside.
Turn the garment inside out and look at the seam. The extra fabric next to the stitching is called the seam allowance.
If there is a wide strip of extra fabric, it can probably be let out. Suit pants often have extra fabric at the back of the waist.
If there is almost no extra fabric, it cannot be let out. Jeans and many cheap clothes have very little.
To make pants longer, look inside the hem. How much fabric is folded up? That is the most you can add.
Warn the customer: the old fold can leave a line that does not press out, especially on jeans and dark fabric.
Say: there is a little extra fabric, our tailor will confirm how much. Or: there is no extra fabric here, so we cannot make it bigger. Be honest. Never guess.
